forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: PWLB borrowing rates expected to fall from 5.6–6.1% to 4.3–4.9% over three years
findings.detail: Treasury advisors' forecasts as at 21 September 2026 project gradual reduction in PWLB borrowing rates over the next three years. Bank Rate is forecast to rise from current 3.75% to 4.00% by December, with subsequent direction described as evenly balanced.
findings.matters: Expected fall in PWLB borrowing costs materially improves the financial outlook if the authority needs to take external borrowing.
findings.figures: PWLB rates currently 5.6–6.1%, forecast 4.3–4.9% over three years; Bank Rate 3.75% forecast to 4.00% by December
findings.quote: PWLB interest rates on borrowing are expected to gradually reduce from the current rates of around 5.6% to 6.1%, depending on the term of the loan to between 4.3% and 4.9% over the next 3 years.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: Police Fund capital programme reduced £7m to £18m; borrowing need £18m, down £6m from original forecast
findings.detail: Police Fund capital programme has fallen from £25m to £18m since the treasury management strategy was approved in March 2026. With no capital resources available, borrowing requirement is £18m, representing a £6m reduction from the original forecast of £24m.
findings.matters: Reduced capital spend and lower borrowing requirement improve the Police Fund's financial position compared to original forecast.
findings.figures: Capital programme £25m reduced to £18m; borrowing need £18m (down from £24m original forecast)
findings.quote: The value of the Police Fund capital programme has fallen from £25m to £18m since the indicator was set in the TM Strategy. As there are no capital resources to fund this there is a borrowing need of £18m.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: MCA capital programme reduced to £255m with no underlying borrowing requirement
findings.detail: Capital programme has been reduced from original estimate of £274m to £255m, with corresponding reduction in capital resources required. MCA requires no external borrowing to fund its programmed capital investment in 2026/27.
findings.matters: Confirms the MCA can fund capital spending from internal resources without incurring new external debt.
findings.figures: Original capital estimate £274m, revised to £255m; capital funding £255m; MCA borrowing need £0m
findings.quote: it remains the case that the MCA has no underlying need to borrow to fund its programmed capital investment in 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: Police grant payment timing change reduces Police Fund investment income forecast to £1.0m from budget of £3.7m
findings.detail: Police grant is now being paid in monthly instalments instead of upfront in April as in prior years. This results in lower cash balances throughout the year, with funds held in lower-yielding money market funds and call accounts rather than fixed-term deposits.
findings.matters: Material change in grant payment timing affects Police Fund cash flow management and liquidity planning throughout the year.
findings.figures: Police Fund investment income forecast £1.0m vs budget £3.7m
findings.quote: When the budget was set it was assumed that the Police grant would be paid up front in April as was the case in 2025/26. Instead, the Police grant is being paid in monthly instalments which has resulted in reduced cash balances and lower investment income.

findings.paper_title: 13i Appendix A - Q1 Treasury Management Update
findings.headline: MCA treasury investment income forecast £17.6m above annual budget
findings.detail: Treasury income was budgeted at £15.4m but is now forecast at £33.0m. The outperformance reflects higher opening balances from 2025/26 underspends, upfront receipt of integrated settlement funds in April 2026, and interest rates exceeding forecast when the budget was set.
findings.matters: Material upside in treasury income reduces pressure on cash flow and external borrowing requirements.
findings.quote: The budgeted treasury income for the year for the MCA is £15.4m and the current forecast is for income of £33.0m so returns are projected to exceed the budgeted treasury investment income for the year by £17.6m.
